+# PAGAN project config. Paths are relative to this file.
+
+# "strict": every sprite uses a palette file from palettes/ (one cohesive look).
+# "open":   sprites may also define their own palette inline.
+palette_mode = "strict"
+
+# Palette for sprites that don't name one. Create one with `pagan new palette <name>`.
+default_palette = "harbor"
+
+# Where `pagan build` writes final assets, e.g. your game engine's asset folder.
+output_dir = "../game/assets/generated"
+
+# Scratch output from `pagan render` / `pagan preview`. Keep it out of version control.
+preview_dir = "previews"
+
+# What `pagan build` produces: PNG sheets + manifest.json always ("png"); add "godot" (SpriteFrames/TileSet .tres),
+# "normals" (normal-map sheets for 3D models, for engine lighting).
+# Every setting here can also be viewed/changed with `pagan config show` / `pagan config set <key> <value>`.
+export = ["png", "godot"]
+
+# Variants (recolours) get their own sheet (+ .tres). Set false when the game recolours in a shader
+# from each variant's "swap" table (base colour -> variant colour) in manifest.json.
+variant_sheets = true
+
+# Smooth (anti-aliased) output for art that isn't pixel art, e.g. sprites the game rotates freely: draw
+# sources at N x the size the game gets, and `pagan build` box-filters them down. 1 = off (pixel-exact).
+supersample = 1
+
+# Bump this when STYLE.md changes in a way that means existing art should be revisited (e.g. "more
+# shadows"). Assets record the style_version they were made under; older ones get lint warning W006.
+# Palette color changes don't need a bump: every asset picks them up automatically.
+style_version = 1
+
+# 3D models (models/*.model.yaml) are rendered with this camera and light, shared by the whole project,
+# so every 3D asset is projected and lit the same way.
+[camera]
+elevation = 42.0      # degrees above the horizon: 90 = straight down, ~30-50 = top-down 3/4 view
+scale = 1           # pixels per voxel
+
+[light]
+direction = [-0.5, 0.45, 0.75]   # towards the light: x right, y up the screen, z up (top-left by default)
+ambient = 0.2                    # brightness of unlit surfaces (0-1); lower = darker shadows, more contrast
+shadows = true                   # parts cast shadows on each other
+shadow_strength = 0.65           # how dark cast shadows are (0-1)
+wrap = 0.3                       # how far light wraps around curves (0-1, higher = softer)
+baked = true                     # false: flat colors for engines with their own lighting (+ export "normals")
+
+# Only with export "godot".
+[godot]
+mipmaps = false                  # import the PNGs with mipmaps (sprites drawn scaled down or rotated)
+filter = "inherit"               # SpriteFrames texture filter: inherit (node/project decides), nearest, linear
+
+[lint]
+# W003: warn when a sprite uses colors from more than this many ramps.
+max_ramps_per_sprite = 3
+# W003 for 3D models, which mix more materials.
+max_ramps_per_model = 6
+# W007: warn when more than this share of pixels changes between consecutive animation frames,
+# even after allowing the whole sprite to move by up to 2px. Keeps animations free of jumps.
+max_frame_change = 0.4
+# W008: most shades an asset may use from one ramp (0 = no limit), e.g. 3 for "3 steps per material".
+max_ramp_steps = 0
+# Warning rule ids to turn off, e.g. ["W001"].
+disable = []
+# Require `outline: auto` on every sprite.
+require_outline = false

+# Art brief
+
+The long-term memory for this project's art: what the game is, what it needs, and decisions made along
+the way. Agents read this (with STYLE.md) before making or changing any asset, and keep it up to date.
+`pagan status` lists what exists; this file says what's *wanted* and why.
+
+## The game
+
+- **Title / working name:** Broadside (working title)
+- **Genre and core loop:** top-down age-of-sail battles for up to 4 players
+- **Perspective:** top-down-3/4 (top-down 3/4, seeing fronts and tops; `[camera] elevation` in pagan.toml)
+- **Rendering style:** pixel art — see STYLE.md
+- **Mood / references:** warm oak and sunlit canvas on a teal sea
+- **Target resolution:** 640x360 scaled x3
+
+## Characters and key assets
+
+For each: what it is, how it looks, sizes, required directions/animations. Example:
+
+- **Player ship** (`models/ship.model.yaml`): two-masted brig, 92x70.
+
+## Asset wishlist
+
+What's still needed, roughly in priority order. Move items to "Done" with the asset name when made.
+
+- [ ] Cannonball, splash, explosion effects
+
+## Done
+
+- (awaiting review) ship
+
+## Decisions and feedback log
+
+Dated notes on what the owner asked for and decided, so later assets stay consistent with it. Example:
+
+- 2026-10-17: "I'm making a sailing game, give me a ship." Defaults used: pixel art, top-down 3/4,
+  palette `harbor`, 8 headings.

@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+# Style bible
+
+The rules that make this project's art look like itself. Agents read this before drawing anything
+and check their previews against it. Replace every **TODO** with a decision; the suggested defaults
+are a reasonable starting point.
+
+Rules that can be checked mechanically belong in `pagan.toml` too (see `[lint]`).
+
+These are **pixel-art** defaults (outline, painted light, shading ramps). For flat / vector-like arcade
+art, they don't apply: start from the flat template instead (`pagan init --style flat`).
+
+## 1. Palette
+
+- Palette file: `palettes/harbor.pal.yaml` (32 colors)
+- Ramp intent — what each ramp is for:
+  - `oak`: hulls and decks; `canvas`: sails; `rope`: rigging, outlines; `red`/`blue`/`green`/`gold`: team colours only; `sea`: water
+
+## 2. Scale
+
+- Base sprite / tile size: 16×16 effects and items
+- Ships: 3D models, 1 px per voxel, hull about 64 voxels long
+- Target base resolution and integer scale: 640×360, ×3
+
+## 3. Outlines
+
+- Style: 1 px dark outline (`0`, tar)
+- Selective outline: no
+
+## 4. Light
+
+- Light direction: top-left
+- Highlights on edges facing the light; the darkest ramp step on the far side.
+
+## 5. Shading
+
+- Ramp steps per material: 3-4
+- No pillow shading (shading that just follows the outline inward from all sides).
+- Dithering: never
+
+## 6. Proportions
+
+- Crew (later): about 1:3
+- Detail level: readable at 1× scale; if a detail is a single isolated pixel, drop it.
+
+## 7. Animation
+
+- Default fps: 6
+- Frame counts: sail 4 (pennants only)
+- Squash and stretch: no
+
+## 8. Do / Don't
+
+Do:
+- Use `mirror: horizontal` for symmetric subjects.
+- Keep silhouettes readable as a solid shape.
+- Keep team colours to flags, gunwales and stripes, so ships stay readable as wood and canvas.
+
+Don't:
+- Flip lit art vertically (`flip: vertical`): the highlights end up on the wrong side. Horizontal flips
+  are fine for symmetric-ish lighting; for strict top-left light, draw or render each direction.
+- Let anything jump between animation frames: the anchor (feet) and unchanged parts must stay on exactly
+  the same pixels. Check the preview's "changes" rows; lint W007 flags large frame-to-frame churn.
+- Use colors outside the palette.
+- Leave orphan pixels (single pixels with no neighbours).
+
+## 9. Reference sprites
+
+The approved sprites that define the look. Compare every new asset against these in preview.
+
+- `models/ship.model.yaml`
+
+## Changelog
+
+Each look change that means existing art should be revisited gets a version (`pagan style bump "note"`
+bumps `style_version` in pagan.toml and adds an entry here, newest first). Assets made under an older
+version get lint warning W006 until they're reviewed and stamped (`pagan mark --current <asset>`).
+Palette edits and `[light]`/`[camera]` changes need no bump for 3D models (they re-render automatically);
+bump when 2D sprites need redrawing to match.
+
+- v1: initial style
